title: Faith That Becomes an Example to Others
summary_text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy thank God for the Thessalonians' active faith, love, and lasting hope in Jesus Christ. They recognize God's choice of these believers because the gospel came with power and the Holy Spirit. Though suffering, the Thessalonians received it with joy and became examples whose faith was widely known. They left idols to serve the true God and await His risen Son, Jesus, who delivers them from coming wrath.
key_points: The writers thank God for the Thessalonians' faith at work, love in service, and enduring hope in Christ.
The gospel came with power and the Holy Spirit, and the believers received it joyfully despite suffering.
Their faith became widely known and set an example for other believers.
They turned from idols to serve God and await Jesus, who delivers them from coming wrath.

title: Paul Recalls His Care and Their Suffering
summary_text: Despite opposition, Paul and his companions preached God's gospel without deceit, greed, or a search for praise. As apostles of Christ, they cared tenderly for the Thessalonians, worked to support themselves, and urged holy and righteous living. Paul thanks God that the believers received their teaching as God's word and endured persecution like the churches in Judea. He condemns opponents who killed Jesus and the prophets and blocked preaching to Gentiles, saying their sins have brought wrath. Paul longs to return, says Satan has hindered him, and calls the believers his joy at Jesus' coming.
key_points: The missionaries boldly preached the gospel to please God, rejecting flattery, greed, and human praise.
They shared their lives, supported themselves, and modeled holy and righteous conduct while encouraging the believers.
The Thessalonians received God's word and suffered from their countrymen as the churches in Judea had suffered.
Paul says opponents obstruct salvation for Gentiles and have filled up their sins, bringing God's wrath.
Satan has blocked Paul's repeated attempts to return to the believers, his hope and joy at Jesus' coming.

title: Timothy's Report Brings Paul Joy
summary_text: Unable to bear his concern any longer, Paul sent Timothy to strengthen the Thessalonians' faith through the gospel of Christ during persecution. He feared the tempter might undo their work, but Timothy returned with good news of their faith, love, and desire to see Paul. Their firm trust in the Lord brings him comfort and great joy amid his own distress. Paul prays to visit, help their faith grow, and see their love increase so they may stand blameless in holiness when Jesus comes with His saints.
key_points: Timothy was sent to strengthen their faith so persecution and temptation would not undo the missionaries' work.
Timothy's good news about their faith and love comforts Paul in his distress.
Paul thanks God with joy and prays earnestly to see them and supply what their faith lacks.
He prays for increasing love and blameless holiness before God when Jesus comes with His saints.

title: Holiness and Hope at the Lord's Coming
summary_text: Paul urges the believers to please God through holiness, avoiding sexual immorality and wronging others, since the Lord punishes such acts. Rejecting this command means rejecting God, who gives His Holy Spirit. They are to grow in love, live quietly, and work for their own needs. Turning to those who have died, Paul gives hope grounded in Jesus' death and rising: the Lord will descend, and the dead in Christ will rise first. Living believers will then join them in the clouds to meet Him and remain with Him forever.
key_points: God calls believers to holiness, including sexual purity and refusing to exploit others.
Paul urges greater love, quiet lives, and work that meets their needs and helps them behave properly toward outsiders.
Jesus' death and rising give hope for those who have died in Him.
The dead in Christ will rise before living believers join them to meet the descending Lord.

title: Staying Awake for the Day of the Lord
summary_text: The Day of the Lord will bring sudden destruction, but Paul tells believers, as people of light, to stay alert with faith, love, and hope. God appointed them for salvation through Jesus Christ rather than wrath, so they are to encourage one another. Paul calls for respect toward leaders, peace, patient help for others, constant prayer, and thanks. They must welcome the Spirit's work, test prophecies, keep what is right, and reject evil. He prays that God will sanctify them completely and keep them blameless until Jesus comes, trusting God's faithfulness.
key_points: The Lord's day comes unexpectedly, so believers must stay alert rather than live in darkness.
Faith, love, and hope of salvation protect those appointed for life with Christ instead of wrath.
Paul calls for respect toward leaders, peace, patience, help for the weak, and good toward everyone.
Believers must rejoice, pray, give thanks, welcome the Spirit, and test prophecies rather than dismiss them.
Paul prays for God to sanctify them wholly, trusting the One who calls them to be faithful.
